column1: Computing Visualizer - Signal Control Workbook
Generated from the running code on 2026-11-21. Every value was read out of the source, not remembered.
WHAT EACH SHEET IS FOR
SIGNALS        all 43 channels: where each one lives in the machine, its kind, and what it drives today
BUSES          the 13 edges of the machine map and the rule that selects each one
ACTS           what ORDINARY WORLD / THE CALL / ORDEAL mean, and the exact threshold behind each
SYNTH          every video-synthesiser knob, its formula, and what it does to the image
COMPUTATIONS   what real tasks look like in telemetry and how you would know one finished
ARCHITECTURE   how a byte actually moves through your Mac, and which stages are invisible
RULES          every rule of layout, shape and movement, with honest provenance
PARAMETERS     every magic number in the renderer, in one place, with derived figures
HOW TO USE IT
Yellow cells are yours. Write in them and I will change the code to match.
Nothing in this workbook is wired to the running visualizer yet - it is a specification, not a control panel.
If you want it live, say so and I will have the renderer read these values from an exported JSON.
THE THREE COLUMNS THAT MATTER MOST
SIGNALS > KIND            decides which DSP is legal. Running an FFT on an event channel is simply wrong.
RULES > PROVENANCE        MEASURED / AUTHORED / INVENTED. Decide about every INVENTED row first.
ARCHITECTURE > VISIBLE    about half the machine produces no unprivileged counter. That is the real constraint.
THE OPEN PROBLEM
macOS has no 'this task is finished' event available without root. The daemon sees rates, never boundaries.
Everything the visualizer says about a task beginning or ending is inference from a channel decaying to baseline.
